did_you_know.text: Did you know? Four sons are listed at the beginning of the genealogy of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.
Did you know? Tola son of Issachar had six sons, who are described as heads of their ancestral families and mighty warriors; in David’s time, they numbered 22,600.
Did you know? The summary of Issachar’s genealogy states that the mighty warriors from all the families of the tribe numbered 87,000.
Did you know? Benjamin’s three sons were Bela, Becher, and Jediael; the chapter then continues by detailing the branches of their families.
Did you know? Among the descendants of Jediael were 17,200 men fit for military service, described as heads of their ancestral families and mighty warriors.
Did you know? The sons of Naphtali mentioned here are Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum, and they were descended from Bilhah.
Did you know? The daughters of Zelophehad are mentioned in the chapter after the account of the family of Manasseh and Machir, preserving their memory in the family genealogy.
Did you know? After the men of Gath killed Ephraim’s sons, he had a son named Beriah because tragedy had struck his household.
Did you know? In these verses, the line of Ephraim continues through Nun to Joshua son of Nun.
Did you know? The list of Asher’s descendants ends by recording 26,000 men fit for military service, described as mighty warriors and heads of the leading clans.
